students.name: Jiwon Kim
students.quote: Students | davejingtian.org davejingtian.org Still got dreams; still got hopes… Skip to content Blog About Publications Students Teaching Python Quotes Sponsors HWS FIA Students NOTE: I am actively looking for talented and motivated students to join my research group. Full RA-ship is available. If you are a student at Purdue and you are interested in my research, feel free to reach me at any time. If you are not a student at Purdue, please apply to the program first and mention my name as your intended advisor. Only then please email me with your research interests and CV. I also provide internship opportunities for doing research with me. You will spend a summer (3 months) at Purdue working with me on some cool projects, and you will be fully funded. Note that internships apply to both domestic and international students. If you are interested in this, please email me with your research interests and CV. I also have a postdoc position available for low-level systems security research. Knowledge of embedded systems, OS kernels, binary analysis, compilers/decompilers, hardware security would be a plus. If you are interested in this, please email me with your research interests and CV. Note: Due to high volume of my emails, I simply could not respond to every email sent to me. But I do check every email sent to me carefully (and hopefully timely). If I find your CV or background interesting, I will reach out to you. Thanks. Note: My student Jiwon Kim is in the job market this year (2026~2027)! If you are looking for a network security researcher with expertise in software defined network (SDN), intent-based network (IBN), and programmable data plane (P4), please check him out. Thanks.

students.name: Jabir Bin Jahangir
students.quote: Jabir Bin Jahangir Jabir received his B.Sc. in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (EEE) from East West University, Bangladesh. Currently, he is a graduate research assistant in the Alam CEED group at Purdue University, West Lafayette, USA. Previously, he was part of the Khan Sustainable Research group at East West University as a research assistant. His research focuses on the computational modeling of photovoltaic systems and solid-state devices. Email: jabir @purdue.edu | Google Scholar | LinkedIn | G itHub Machine Learning
students.note: Whole student/role/alumni section reviewed; no one-student cutoff.

students.name: In Huh
students.quote: In Huh In Huh is a Ph.D. student in the Alam CEED group at Purdue University, USA, and a staff research engineer at Samsung Electronics, South Korea. He earned his B.Sc. and M.Sc. in Electronic Engineering from Sogang University, South Korea. His research interests focus on the theoretical foundations of physics-inspired machine learning methods, particularly through the lens of symmetry and geometry, and their practical applications in nanoelectronics engineering. Email: ihuh @purdue.edu | Google Scholar | LinkedIn Reliability Physics
students.note: Whole student/role/alumni section reviewed; no one-student cutoff.

students.name: Mir Md Fahimul Islam
students.quote: Mir Md Fahimul Islam Fahim obtained his B.Sc. (2018) and M.Sc. (2020) in Electrical and Electronic Engineering from University of Dhaka, Bangladesh. His academic excellence during undergraduate studies secured him the dean's award and NST fellowship. In Fall 2023, he joined Alam CEED group for his PhD. His research interests include the reliability of next-generation oxide transistors under extreme conditions. His prior research involved the simulation and modeling of negative capacitance transistors intended for use in biosensing and logic applications. Prior to joining Purdue University as a researcher, he worked as a lecturer at the University of Dhaka in Bangladesh. LinkedIn Email: islam93@purdue.edu Google Scholar
students.note: Whole student/role/alumni section reviewed; no one-student cutoff.

students.name: Chun-An Shih
students.quote: Chun-An Shih Chun-An received his B.Sc. in Nano Science and Engineering in 2019 and completed his M.Sc. at the International College of Semiconductor Technology, National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University, Taiwan, in 2022. In the fall of 2023, he joined the CEED group as a Ph.D. student in Electrical Engineering. Prior to this, he was an intern at Imec from 2021 to 2022, focusing on ESD HBM characterization on GaN-on-Si devices. His current research interests include the reliability and characterization of next-generation oxide transistors. LinkedIn Email: shih72@purdue.edu Google Scholar

students.name: Yi-Chieh Chen
students.quote: Yi-Chieh Chen Yi-Chieh gained her B.S. degree from National Tsing Hua University, Taiwan and completed her M.S. degree at Graduate Institution of Electronics Engineering from National Taiwan University, Taiwan. Her M.S. study is mainly about the experimental characteristics of GeSn/Oxide interfaces and first principle calculation. Before joining CEED group at Purdue in Fall 2024 as a PhD student, she worked as a research assistant at National Cheng Kung University, Taiwan from 2023 to 2024. Email : chen5239@purdue.edu Biosensors

students.name: Yeasin Arafat Pritom
students.quote: Yeasin Arafat Pritom Yeasin is a PhD researcher in the CEED research group at Purdue University ((since Spring 2026)). He completed his BSc (2024) in Electrical and Electronic Engineering from the University of Dhaka, Bangladesh. During his undergraduate studies, he received the IEEE Electron Devices Society Undergraduate Fellowship (Region 10, 2023), becoming the first recipient from Bangladesh. His research focuses on physics-based modeling of microfluidic systems and biosensors, with emphasis on multiphysics and device-level simulation. His previous work includes physics and machine learning-based modeling of emerging electronic devices, including negative capacitance FETs, forksheet FETs and photovoltaic solar cells. Before joining Purdue University as a researcher, he served as a Lecturer at BRAC University, Dhaka, Bangladesh. Linkedin Google Scholar Email: ypritom@purdue.edu

students.name: Yuanrui Chen
students.quote: Ph.D. Students (alphabetized by last name) Yuanrui Chen chen4387@purdue Yuanrui Chen joined the group in 2022 as a first-year Ph.D. student in ECE. His current research is related to metasurfaces. Hailing from Chengdu, China, known for its cuisine, Yuanrui completed his undergraduate studies at UIUC. Beyond his scientific pursuits, he developed a deep fascination for history and geography, often exploring diverse cultures through travel. He also likes rock music, soccer and aquatic sports. Juhee Han juheehan @purdue Juhee joined the group as a Ph.D. student in ECE in Fall 2026. She got a bachelor's degree in Electronic and Electrical Engineering from Sungkyunkwan University. Her research interests lie in computational imaging, artificial intelligence, and optics-computation co-design. During free time, She enjoys staying active by swimming and playing tennis. Yuxuan Liu liu3910@purdue Yuxuan joined the group in 2023. Born in Changchun, China, he received his bachelor's degree in Optical Engineering from Zhejiang University and is now conducting experiments in computational imaging and application of metasurface. Outside the lab, Yuxuan is interested in soccer and basketball. [ Website ] Junjie Luo luo330@purdue Junjie Luo, a PhD student in Prof Guo's research group, hails from Shenzhen, a city situated adjacent to Hong Kong. During his leisure time, he takes pleasure in repairing computers, cooking, engaging in weightlifting, and reading literature spanning various genres and periods. [ Website ] Wei Xu xu1639@purdue Wei is passionate about improving the efficiency and accuracy of computer vision through the application of numerical analysis and machine learning methods. He earned his bachelor's degree from Tianjin University (China) and pursued his master's degree at Northeastern University. When he's not immersed in his research, Wei loves to embark on hiking adventures, exploring the beauty of nature. [ Website ]

students.quote: Ph.D. Students (alphabetized by last name) Yuanrui Chen chen4387@purdue Yuanrui Chen joined the group in 2022 as a first-year Ph.D. student in ECE. His current research is related to metasurfaces. Hailing from Chengdu, China, known for its cuisine, Yuanrui completed his undergraduate studies at UIUC. Beyond his scientific pursuits, he developed a deep fascination for history and geography, often exploring diverse cultures through travel. He also likes rock music, soccer and aquatic sports. Juhee Han juheehan @purdue Juhee joined the group as a Ph.D. student in ECE in Fall 2026. She got a bachelor's degree in Electronic and Electrical Engineering from Sungkyunkwan University. Her research interests lie in computational imaging, artificial intelligence, and optics-computation co-design. During free time, She enjoys staying active by swimming and playing tennis. Yuxuan Liu liu3910@purdue Yuxuan joined the group in 2023. Born in Changchun, China, he received his bachelor's degree in Optical Engineering from Zhejiang University and is now conducting experiments in computational imaging and application of metasurface. Outside the lab, Yuxuan is interested in soccer and basketball. [ Website ] Junjie Luo luo330@purdue Junjie Luo, a PhD student in Prof Guo's research group, hails from Shenzhen, a city situated adjacent to Hong Kong. During his leisure time, he takes pleasure in repairing computers, cooking, engaging in weightlifting, and reading literature spanning various genres and periods. [ Website ] Wei Xu xu1639@purdue Wei is passionate about improving the efficiency and accuracy of computer vision through the application of numerical analysis and machine learning methods. He earned his bachelor's degree from Tianjin University (China) and pursued his master's degree at Northeastern University. When he's not immersed in his research, Wei loves to embark on hiking adventures, exploring the beauty of nature. [ Website ]

Show More Research Interests I am interested in developing scalable, reliable and efficient probabilistic methods for machine learning and generative AI. Our work bridges theoretical foundations and practical implementations, aiming to address fundamental challenges in building trustworthy and efficient AI systems. Currently, I focus on the following key directions: (1) alignment and safety of foundation models, including LLMs, VLMs, and diffusion models; (2) Probabilistic inference, uncertainty estimation, and Bayesian methods; and (3) Generation and learning on discrete data. Show More Research Interests I am interested in developing scalable, reliable and efficient probabilistic methods for machine learning and generative AI. Our work bridges theoretical foundations and practical implementations, aiming to address fundamental challenges in building trustworthy and efficient AI systems. Currently, I focus on the following key directions: (1) alignment and safety of foundation models, including LLMs, VLMs, and diffusion models; (2) Probabilistic inference, uncertainty estimation, and Bayesian methods; and (3) Generation and learning on discrete data. Show More Research Interests I am interested in developing scalable, reliable and efficient probabilistic methods for machine learning and generative AI. Our work bridges theoretical foundations and practical implementations, aiming to address fundamental challenges in building trustworthy and efficient AI systems. Currently, I focus on the following key directions: (1) alignment and safety of foundation models, including LLMs, VLMs, and diffusion models; (2) Probabilistic inference, uncertainty estimation, and Bayesian methods; and (3) Generation and learning on discrete data. Show More Research Interests I am interested in developing scalable, reliable and efficient probabilistic methods for machine learning and generative AI. Our work bridges theoretical foundations and practical implementations, aiming to address fundamental challenges in building trustworthy and efficient AI systems. Currently, I focus on the following key directions: (1) alignment and safety of foundation models, including LLMs, VLMs, and diffusion models; (2) Probabilistic inference, uncertainty estimation, and Bayesian methods; and (3) Generation and learning on discrete data. students.name: Appal Badi
students.quote: Current Students Graduate Appal Badi Doctor of Technology (D.Tech.) | Focus Area: Data and Cloud Observability Appal is a Doctor of Technology (D.Tech) student at Purdue University. He is the Head of Data Products at Silicon Valley Bank, CA. He has an MBA from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, a graduate certificate in cloud computing from Austin University and a Bachelor’s in computer science from India. He has over 20 years of experience in various roles, including leadership positions in Information Technology and Data Science in different companies across the globe. He has extensive experience building and managing complex data warehouses, data governance and cloud platforms to support internal/external reporting and analytics needs for organizations. He also worked on process optimization for organizations using various analytical tools. His research interests are in data and cloud observability. Linkedin-in Github Ayush Shridhar M.S. (Type: Proceedings Article | Abstract | Links | BibTeX ) @inproceedings{10227727, title = {Heuristic-based Resource Allocation for Cloud-native Machine Learning Workloads}, author = {Ayush Shridhar and Deepak Nadig}, url = {https://deepaknadig.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/Heuristic-based_Resource_Allocation_for_Cloud-native_Machine_Learning_Workloads.pdf}, doi = {10.1109/ANTS56424.2022.10227727}, issn = {2153-1684}, year = {2022}, date = {2022-12-01}, urldate = {2022-12-01}, booktitle = {2022 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)}, pages = {415-418}, abstract = {As machine learning workloads become computationally demanding, there is an increased focus on distributed machine learning to train and deploy models across multiple machines in a cloud-native cluster. However, optimizing a machine learning model’s lifecycle to facilitate efficient resource utilization is still an active area of research. The approach typically involves a manual effort to partition the models into distinct layers and decide how to store these distinct layers on a distributed computing framework. However, distributing distinct layers across nodes can induce a network latency bottleneck in the machine learning pipeline. Further, the above process becomes more inefficient as models become increasingly complex. In this paper, we present a heuristic-based approach to distributed model training. Further, we analyze the resource utilization metrics from a sample machine learning pipeline deployed on a KubeFlow MLOps framework testbed.}, keywords = {}, pubstate = {published}, tppubtype = {inproceedings} } Close As machine learning workloads become computationally demanding, there is an increased focus on distributed machine learning to train and deploy models across multiple machines in a cloud-native cluster. However, optimizing a machine learning model’s lifecycle to facilitate efficient resource utilization is still an active area of research. The approach typically involves a manual effort to partition the models into distinct layers and decide how to store these distinct layers on a distributed computing framework. However, distributing distinct layers across nodes can induce a network latency bottleneck in the machine learning pipeline. Further, the above process becomes more inefficient as models become increasingly complex. In this paper, we present a heuristic-based approach to distributed model training. Further, we analyze the resource utilization metrics from a sample machine learning pipeline deployed on a KubeFlow MLOps framework testbed. Close https://deepaknadig.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/Heuristic-based_Resource_Allo[...] doi:10.1109/ANTS56424.2022.10227727 Close Isham Jitender Mahajan M.S. (Thesis) | Focus Area: Cloud-native Auotscaling Isham Mahajan is a Master’s student in Computer and Information Technology at Purdue University. He has a Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology from the Manipal Institute of Technology, India. He was a Graduate Research Assistant at Purdue’s Rosen Center for Advanced Computing (RCAC), where he automated and optimized JupyterHub deployments on Kubernetes. Isham’s research interests lie in the economic aspect of cloud technology, specifically in reducing deployment costs by fine-tuning container resources within Kubernetes. He is also passionate about creating efficient, cost-effective solutions for cloud application developers. Linkedin-in Github Karumuri Meher Hasanth M.S. (Thesis) | Focus Area: Network Service Mesh Hasanth is a Master’s student in Computers and Information Technology at Purdue University. His research interests are cloud-native network service mesh (NSM) and NSM performance optimization. Hasanth was an intern at Samsung, where he worked on DevOps pipelines. Before joining Purdue, he worked as a Site Reliability Engineer at ADP, acquiring skills in system reliability, availability, and performance enhancement. His current expertise is DevOps, Kubernetes, cloud technologies (AWS), and Python automation. He has a Bachelor’s degree in Electronics and Communication Engineering from Vellore Institute of Technology, India. Linkedin-in Github Shoaib Basu M.S. (Thesis) | Focus Area: Cloud Accelerators Shoaib is a Master’s student in Computer and Information Technology at Purdue University. His research interests are in Cloud Accelerators and network offloading. Linkedin-in Github Kevin Wesley Kusiak M.S. (Thesis) | Focus Area: Cloud Security Kevin is a Master’s student in Computer and Information Technology at Purdue University. His research interests are in cloud security and quantum networking. He has over 3 years of experience in the mobile security field, and is currently employed in a full-time position as a security researcher at Peraton Labs. Linkedin-in Github Rohit Balasaheb Bankar M.S. (Thesis) | Focus Area: Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) Rohit is a Master’s student in Computer and Information Technology at Purdue University. He holds a Bachelor’s degree from IIT Indore, India. Before joining Purdue, He worked as a Software Development Engineer at Razorpay, where he specialized in big data systems and acquired skills in Scala, Spark, Kafka, Golang, and Java, with experience in engineering large Scala data-intensive systems. His research interests are in AI/ML for Software-Defined Networking (SDN) and cloud-native MLOps. Linkedin-in Github Vivek Karunai Kiri Ragavan M.S. (Thesis) | Focus Area: Cloud Schedulers Vivek is pursuing a Master’s degree in Computers and Information Technology at Purdue University. He serves as a Graduate Professional Assistant at Purdue’s Rosen Center for Advanced Computing (RCAC), where he is engaged in the development of Ticket Hub, an AI-driven full-stack application focused on the deep analysis of user support requests. Prior to joining Purdue, Vivek gained experience as a Software Consulting Engineer at Cisco Systems, India, working in the Software Automation and Orchestration Team. His current areas of expertise include Kubernetes, Cloud Technologies (AWS and Azure), MERN Stack and Python Automation. He holds a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science and Engineering from Amrita School of Engineering, India. Vivek’s research interests revolve around Kubernetes Schedulers and Cloud Native Infrastructure. Linkedin-in Github Parv Dani M.S. (Thesis) | Focus Area: Cloud Schedulers Parv is a Master’s student in Computer and Information Technology at Purdue University. His research interests are in enhancing cloud security using eBPF and XDP. He has have previously worked at Oracle Cloud Infrastructure in the highly scalable cloud service development team in Bangalore, India. He has a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science from the Birla Institute of Technology, Pilani, India. His other interests include soccer, music, reading and he is passionate about health and fitness. (Type: Proceedings Article | Abstract | Links | BibTeX ) @inproceedings{10227727, title = {Heuristic-based Resource Allocation for Cloud-native Machine Learning Workloads}, author = {Ayush Shridhar and Deepak Nadig}, url = {https://deepaknadig.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/Heuristic-based_Resource_Allocation_for_Cloud-native_Machine_Learning_Workloads.pdf}, doi = {10.1109/ANTS56424.2022.10227727}, issn = {2153-1684}, year = {2022}, date = {2022-12-01}, urldate = {2022-12-01}, booktitle = {2022 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)}, pages = {415-418}, abstract = {As machine learning workloads become computationally demanding, there is an increased focus on distributed machine learning to train and deploy models across multiple machines in a cloud-native cluster. However, optimizing a machine learning model’s lifecycle to facilitate efficient resource utilization is still an active area of research. The approach typically involves a manual effort to partition the models into distinct layers and decide how to store these distinct layers on a distributed computing framework. However, distributing distinct layers across nodes can induce a network latency bottleneck in the machine learning pipeline. Further, the above process becomes more inefficient as models become increasingly complex. In this paper, we present a heuristic-based approach to distributed model training. Further, we analyze the resource utilization metrics from a sample machine learning pipeline deployed on a KubeFlow MLOps framework testbed.}, keywords = {}, pubstate = {published}, tppubtype = {inproceedings} } Close As machine learning workloads become computationally demanding, there is an increased focus on distributed machine learning to train and deploy models across multiple machines in a cloud-native cluster. However, optimizing a machine learning model’s lifecycle to facilitate efficient resource utilization is still an active area of research. The approach typically involves a manual effort to partition the models into distinct layers and decide how to store these distinct layers on a distributed computing framework. However, distributing distinct layers across nodes can induce a network latency bottleneck in the machine learning pipeline. Further, the above process becomes more inefficient as models become increasingly complex. In this paper, we present a heuristic-based approach to distributed model training. Further, we analyze the resource utilization metrics from a sample machine learning pipeline deployed on a KubeFlow MLOps framework testbed. (Thesis) | Focus Area: Cloud-native Auotscaling Isham Mahajan is a Master’s student in Computer and Information Technology at Purdue University. He has a Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology from the Manipal Institute of Technology, India. He was a Graduate Research Assistant at Purdue’s Rosen Center for Advanced Computing (RCAC), where he automated and optimized JupyterHub deployments on Kubernetes. Isham’s research interests lie in the economic aspect of cloud technology, specifically in reducing deployment costs by fine-tuning container resources within Kubernetes. He is also passionate about creating efficient, cost-effective solutions for cloud application developers. Linkedin-in Github Karumuri Meher Hasanth M.S. (Thesis) | Focus Area: Network Service Mesh Hasanth is a Master’s student in Computers and Information Technology at Purdue University. His research interests are cloud-native network service mesh (NSM) and NSM performance optimization. Hasanth was an intern at Samsung, where he worked on DevOps pipelines. Before joining Purdue, he worked as a Site Reliability Engineer at ADP, acquiring skills in system reliability, availability, and performance enhancement. His current expertise is DevOps, Kubernetes, cloud technologies (AWS), and Python automation. He has a Bachelor’s degree in Electronics and Communication Engineering from Vellore Institute of Technology, India. Linkedin-in Github Shoaib Basu M.S. (Thesis) | Focus Area: Cloud Accelerators Shoaib is a Master’s student in Computer and Information Technology at Purdue University. His research interests are in Cloud Accelerators and network offloading. Linkedin-in Github Kevin Wesley Kusiak M.S. (Thesis) | Focus Area: Cloud Security Kevin is a Master’s student in Computer and Information Technology at Purdue University. His research interests are in cloud security and quantum networking. He has over 3 years of experience in the mobile security field, and is currently employed in a full-time position as a security researcher at Peraton Labs. Linkedin-in Github Rohit Balasaheb Bankar M.S. (Thesis) | Focus Area: Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) Rohit is a Master’s student in Computer and Information Technology at Purdue University. He holds a Bachelor’s degree from IIT Indore, India. Before joining Purdue, He worked as a Software Development Engineer at Razorpay, where he specialized in big data systems and acquired skills in Scala, Spark, Kafka, Golang, and Java, with experience in engineering large Scala data-intensive systems. His research interests are in AI/ML for Software-Defined Networking (SDN) and cloud-native MLOps. Linkedin-in Github Vivek Karunai Kiri Ragavan M.S. (Thesis) | Focus Area: Cloud Schedulers Vivek is pursuing a Master’s degree in Computers and Information Technology at Purdue University. He serves as a Graduate Professional Assistant at Purdue’s Rosen Center for Advanced Computing (RCAC), where he is engaged in the development of Ticket Hub, an AI-driven full-stack application focused on the deep analysis of user support requests. Prior to joining Purdue, Vivek gained experience as a Software Consulting Engineer at Cisco Systems, India, working in the Software Automation and Orchestration Team. His current areas of expertise include Kubernetes, Cloud Technologies (AWS and Azure), MERN Stack and Python Automation. He holds a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science and Engineering from Amrita School of Engineering, India. Vivek’s research interests revolve around Kubernetes Schedulers and Cloud Native Infrastructure. Linkedin-in Github Parv Dani M.S. (Thesis) | Focus Area: Cloud Schedulers Parv is a Master’s student in Computer and Information Technology at Purdue University. His research interests are in enhancing cloud security using eBPF and XDP. He has have previously worked at Oracle Cloud Infrastructure in the highly scalable cloud service development team in Bangalore, India. He has a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science from the Birla Institute of Technology, Pilani, India. His other interests include soccer, music, reading and he is passionate about health and fitness. students.name: Harshini Magesh
students.quote: Team Members Weiruo Zhang Assistant Professor Weiruo earned her Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering from Stanford University. For her doctoral study, she worked with Dr. David Dill in Computer Science of Stanford University, developing graph based machine learning (ML) algorithms for metabolomics data. Weiruo later worked with Dr. Sylvia Plevritis in Stanford School of medicine, with research focus of implementing ML/AI approaches to integrate multi-modality data to study tumor progression. Outside the lab, she enjoys piano, reading, oil painting, and watching soccer. Harshini Magesh Undergraduate student Harshini is a senior majoring in Computer Science with a concentration in Machine Intelligence and a minor in Mathematics at Purdue University. Her research interests center on leveraging machine learning and computational modeling to advance data-driven discovery in biology and medicine. Outside of research, Harshini enjoys singing, music production and exploring the creative applications of technology. Yunyi Gao Graduate student Yunyi is currently a Computer Science (CS) graduate student at Tufts University. Yunyi completed her Undergraduate studies in CS at Purdue, during which she worked in our lab as a research assistant. Yunyi continues working with us currently on a spatial multi-omics integration project. Kyenret Yakubu Ayuba PhD student Kyenret is a PhD student in the PULSe program. She earned her B.S. in Biomedical Engineering from Purdue University. Her research includes developing machine learning and molecular simulation pipelines for protein interactions and drug discovery, as well as computational and statistical approaches to investigate gene-environment interactions in admixed populations. In her free time, she enjoys reading and watching movies and documentaries. Harsha Srirangam Undergraduate student Harsha is a second-year undergraduate student studying Applied Mathematics and Computer Science. His previous work spans natural language processing, computer vision, computational biology, and cancer metabolomics, and he is more broadly interested in developing biological foundation models with multi-omic data. In his free time, he enjoys playing basketball, watching and reading sci-fi, and making origami. Md. Ishrak Ahsan PhD student Ishrak is a PhD student in Computer Science. He received his B.Sc. in Computer Science and Engineering from the Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET).
